answer:
**Answer:** The interaction between BCG vaccination status and prior medical history on COVID-19 severity is not statistically distinguishable from no interaction. In the primary proportional-odds ordinal logistic regression of the derived 0–4 COVID-19 severity outcome on BCG status, prior medical history, their interaction, and patient interaction frequency (patients_seen), the interaction odds ratio is **OR = 1.26 (95% CI 0.65–2.47; p = 0.49)** — i.e., a BCG×history interaction OR of ~1.3 in the direction of BCG being associated with *worse* (not better) severity among subjects with prior medical history, but with a confidence interval that comfortably includes 1.0. Prior medical history itself is significantly associated with higher severity (OR 1.66, 95% CI 1.03–2.66, p=0.036), as is patient interaction frequency (OR 1.66 per step, 95% CI 1.24–2.22, p<0.001); the BCG main effect is null (OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.55–1.62).

**Assumptions stated explicitly:** (a) MHORRES is coded 1 = No, 2 = Yes (inferred; corroborated by MHONGO/MHCM "Yes" appearing only on MHORRES=2 rows and by zero positives for transplant/immunodeficiency items). (b) The 44 COVID AE rows missing AESEV (41 subjects) were imputed from AEOUT/AESER as: AESER=Yes or AEOUT=Worse → 3; Unchanged → 2; Resolved/Improved → 1 (resulting levels: 32→1, 8→2, 1→3).

**Primary model (n=1000; outcome 0=no COVID AE, 1–4=max COVID AESEV):**
| Term | β | OR | 95% CI | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BCG | −0.059 | 0.94 | 0.55–1.62 | 0.83 |
| priorMH | 0.507 | 1.66 | 1.03–2.66 | 0.036 |
| BCG×priorMH | 0.235 | **1.26** | 0.65–2.47 | 0.49 |
| patients_seen (0/1/2) | 0.506 | 1.66 | 1.24–2.22 | <0.001 |

Cell counts (arm × history × severity 0/1/2/3/4): BCG, no history: 186/15/13/1/0; BCG, history: 216/32/26/7/4; Placebo, no history: 186/17/15/0/0; Placebo, history: 223/20/36/1/2.

**Sensitivity analyses (interaction OR, 95% CI):** complete-case excluding the 41 imputed subjects (n=956): 1.33 (0.61–2.88); COVID cases only, levels 1–4 (n=189): 0.88 (0.26–2.92); severe-comorbidity-only history definition (n=263 positives): 0.61 (0.31–1.20); Age/SEX-adjusted: 1.23 (0.62–2.41); using expect_interact instead of patients_seen: 1.32 (0.68–2.59). Every variant's 95% CI includes 1.

**Imprecision flag:** the severe tail is very sparse — only 6 subjects at severity 4 and 9 at severity 3 overall (BCG/history cell holds 4 of the 6 fatal-level cases), so the interaction estimate at the upper end of the severity scale is unstable and the proportional-odds interaction OR should be read as an average across thresholds. Overall conclusion: no evidence of an interaction between BCG vaccination and prior medical history on COVID-19 severity once patient interaction frequency is controlled; both history (OR≈1.7) and patient-contact frequency (OR≈1.7) independently raise the odds of more severe outcomes.
